d: Weatherhaven starts in British Columbia, serving the expedition and mining exploration markets.
The first contract with the Canadian military, and the launch of the MEX-26 helicopter maintenance shelter.
The first Antarctic camp, built with the Polarhaven shelter — followed by contracts with more than 10 countries.
An Arctic camp redeployed to the demilitarized zone between Kuwait and Iraq — the start of a UN partnership that continues today.
The first Mobile Expandable Container Configurations go to US Natick Labs and the Canadian Coast Guard.
A 1,400-person Relocatable Temporary Camp deployed to Kosovo.
A 2,200-person camp supplied to support Canadian Forces in Afghanistan.
Emergency camps for 3,100 people delivered to the Peruvian Navy.
The beginning of a new era for the company.
Canada awards the Medium Support Vehicle System baseline shelters program to DEW Engineering and teaming partner Weatherhaven.
A softwall field hospital standing offer in Australia, won against 11 international bidders — and emergency shelters for UN and Brazilian relief efforts in Haiti.
Named one of the Top 50 Canadian defence companies by Canadian Defence Review for the first time.
A contract from Boeing for 24 MSVS Special Equipment Shelter kits for CH-147 Chinook maintenance — and 2nd place for BC Business Innovator of the Year.
The Tactical Redeployable Expanding Container Capability patent is filed.
Weatherhaven is awarded Canada’s Headquarters Shelter System acquisition and in-service support contracts, worth $167M CDN.
Weatherhaven field hospitals support the pandemic response in Chile and across Latin America.
A partnering agreement announced at Land Forces 2026 in Perth to support defence, emergency response, research and humanitarian programs across the Asia-Pacific.
